title: Captured restoration bound
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $c_0$ be a configuration on input $x$, let $p$ be an input-head position, and let $t$ be a natural number. Suppose the machine is not halted at any time $j<t$ when started from $c_0$. Then there is a time $r \le 2t+1$ at which the clean wrapper, started in its captured restoration checkpoint for the time-$t$ configuration and its recorded history, reaches the administrative configuration whose source work fields are restored to those of $c_0$, whose retained word is the output after $t$ steps, whose control is in restoration phase, whose input head is at $p$, whose capture head is at the length of that output, and whose output is empty.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
for every $j<t$, the configuration reached after $j$ steps from $c_0$ is not halted
replaced:
If the source $M$ is live for $t$ steps from $c_0$, then within $2t + 1$ steps the
clean wrapper's captured restoration, started at the checkpoint of the time-$t$
configuration with its history, reaches the administrative configuration in which
the original source work fields of $c_0$ are restored, the time-$t$ output is
retained on the last tape, and the capture head stands at the end of that word.
